+type HTTPStatusError struct {
+	StatusCode int
+	Status     metav1.Status
+}
+
+func (e HTTPStatusError) Error() string {
+	return fmt.Sprintf("HTTP Status Error %d: %s", e.StatusCode, e.Status.Message)
+}
+
+// ApplyTransport implements TransportFault by returning a synthetic API error response.
+func (e HTTPStatusError) ApplyTransport() *HTTPStatusError {
+	return &e
+}
+
+// NewHTTPStatusError creates an HTTPStatusError representing common API server failures.
+func NewHTTPStatusError(statusCode int, reason metav1.StatusReason, message string) HTTPStatusError {
+	return HTTPStatusError{
+		StatusCode: statusCode,
+		Status: metav1.Status{
+			TypeMeta: metav1.TypeMeta{
+				Kind:       "Status",
+				APIVersion: "v1",
+			},
+			Status:  metav1.StatusFailure,
+			Message: message,
+			Reason:  reason,
+			Code:    int32(statusCode),
+		},
+	}
+}
+
+// FaultInjectingTransport wraps http.RoundTripper and triggers faults on matching REST API calls.
+type FaultInjectingTransport struct {
+	realTransport http.RoundTripper
+	registry      *FaultRegistry
+	activity      *activityTracker // may be nil; records mutating traffic for settle detection
+	resolver      *request.RequestInfoFactory
+}
+
+// NewFaultInjectingTransport creates a wrapped http.RoundTripper that routes request
+// hooks to the registry. activity may be nil when settle detection is not needed.
+func NewFaultInjectingTransport(realTransport http.RoundTripper, registry *FaultRegistry, activity *activityTracker) http.RoundTripper {
+	return &FaultInjectingTransport{
+		realTransport: realTransport,
+		registry:      registry,
+		activity:      activity,
+		resolver: &request.RequestInfoFactory{
+			APIPrefixes:          sets.NewString("api", "apis"),
+			GrouplessAPIPrefixes: sets.NewString("api"),
+		},
+	}
+}
+
+func (t *FaultInjectingTransport) RoundTrip(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
+	info, _ := t.resolver.NewRequestInfo(req)
+	if info == nil || !info.IsResourceRequest {
+		return t.realTransport.RoundTrip(req)
+	}
+
+	switch req.Method {
+	case http.MethodPost, http.MethodPut, http.MethodPatch, http.MethodDelete:
+		t.activity.recordMutation()
+	}
+
+	if httpErr := t.registry.ResolveTransport(req.Context(), ClientFacts{
+		Verb:        req.Method,
+		Group:       info.APIGroup,
+		Resource:    info.Resource,
+		Subresource: info.Subresource,
+		Namespace:   info.Namespace,
+		Name:        info.Name,
+	}); httpErr != nil {
+		return synthesizeResponse(*httpErr)

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Question on the mechanism. I traced grpc-go v1.81.0 (the version kubernetes vendors) to check what happens when the plugin side closes the connection during a long RegisterPlugin:

1. When a READY connection is lost, the channel goes IDLE and installs an idlePicker, it does not break permanently: [pickfirst.go#L687](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.81.0/balancer/pickfirst/pickfirst.go#L687) and [L704](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.81.0/balancer/pickfirst/pickfirst.go#L704)
2. The next RPC on the old client kicks the channel into reconnecting on the same socket path: [pickfirst.go#L867](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.81.0/balancer/pickfirst/pickfirst.go#L867)
3. While it reconnects, even fail fast RPCs block rather than fail, since pick loops on ErrNoSubConnAvailable: [picker_wrapper.go#L159](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.81.0/picker_wrapper.go#L159)

So if the socket file still exists at notify time, the old client reconnects and delivers the notification by itself. And if the socket is gone, the fresh dial here fails too, giving the same cleanup and retry as before.

The case where the re-dial genuinely helps is a socket that disappears and then reappears: a failed connect puts the channel in TRANSIENT_FAILURE ([pickfirst.go#L753](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.81.0/balancer/pickfirst/pickfirst.go#L753)) and a fail fast RPC during the 1s+ backoff window ([backoff.go#L48](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.81.0/backoff/backoff.go#L48)) gets Unavailable immediately: [picker_wrapper.go#L176](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.81.0/picker_wrapper.go#L176). But `grpc.WaitForReady(true)` on the NotifyRegistrationStatus call covers that too ([picker_wrapper.go#L172](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.81.0/picker_wrapper.go#L172)), without a second connection and without every successful registration paying an extra dial.

Did you reproduce the failure and confirm the fresh dial succeeds where the old client fails? Asking because the fix rests on that premise.

We vendor v1.81.1, not v1.81.0, but I checked the actual vendored source and the pickfirst/picker_wrapper mechanism you traced matches almost line-for-line. Rather than defend the re-dial, switched to grpc.WaitForReady(true) on the notify call in d33d4dbef86 . it covers the TRANSIENT_FAILURE fail-fast gap you identified without a second connection. Thanks for tracing this through, it's a better fix.

+	defer c.streamsMu.Unlock()
+	return c.streams[id]

+	c.streamsMu.Lock()
+	defer c.streamsMu.Unlock()
+	c.streams[id] = s
+}
+
+func (c *wsStreamCreator) removeStream(s httpstream.Stream) {
+	c.streamsMu.Lock()
+	defer c.streamsMu.Unlock()
+	id := byte(s.Identifier())
+	delete(c.streams, id)
+}

+// CreateStream uses id from passed headers to create a stream over "c.conn" connection.
+// Returns a Stream structure or nil and an error if one occurred.
+func (c *wsStreamCreator) CreateStream(headers http.Header) (httpstream.Stream, error) {
+	streamType := headers.Get(v1.StreamType)
+	id, ok := streamType2streamID[streamType]
+	if !ok {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown stream type: %s", streamType)
+	}
+	if s := c.getStream(id); s != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("duplicate stream for type %s", streamType)

+	reader, writer := io.Pipe()

+		readPipe:      reader,
+		writePipe:     writer,
+		conn:          c.conn,
+		connWriteLock: &c.connWriteLock,
+		id:            id,
+	}
+	c.setStream(id, s)

+func (c *wsStreamCreator) Close() error {
+	c.closeAllStreamReaders(nil)

discussion_comments.comment_body: Yes--they are the same. The `pingPeriod` is how often the heartbeat/ping is sent, while the `heartbeatDeadline` is the overall deadline to consider the connection dead.
